title: The open-source IFC toolchain centers on ifcopenshell
content:
The open-source toolchain for working with IFC files (BIM briefing):

- **ifcopenshell** — "what everyone uses"; the core IFC library. Notably ships an MCP server (docs.ifcopenshell.org/ifcmcp.html), making IFC directly accessible to agents. Speckle partially uses it under the hood.
- **bimserver** (opensourcebim/bimserver) — open-source BIM server
- **Bonsai** — Blender plugin for BIM authoring/viewing (extensions.blender.org); with sample IFC files from buildingSMART's test suite
- **ifc-bench** (huggingface.co/datasets/sylvainHellin/ifc-bench) — benchmark dataset for evaluating BIM comprehension in AI systems: curated IFC models with QA pairs across 4 complexity categories
- **cobbie** (github.com/sylvainHellin/cobbie) — Code-Based BIM Information Extraction, same author

Pipeline-relevant contact: Peter Kombolschek (via Jakob) is releasing an open-source **IFC viewer and editor supporting 4D (time) and 5D (costs)**. A well-known Austrian architect who works on BIM norms — potentially both a tool source and a distribution channel.
description: ifcopenshell is 'what everyone uses' (incl. an MCP server); around it: bimserver, Bonsai for Blender, ifc-bench + cobbie for AI evaluation, and an upcoming open-source 4D/5D IFC editor.
